residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been a bona fide resident of Pennsylvania for at least six months before filing the divorce complaint.

mutualConsent.description: 90-day waiting period from date of service of complaint (mutual consent divorce under § 3301(c)). Both parties must file Affidavits of Consent after 90 days.

separation.description: 1-year separation period for unilateral no-fault divorce under § 3301(d) (as amended effective December 2016, reduced from 2 years to 1 year). One party may file unilaterally after 1 year of separation.

noFault.name: Mutual Consent
noFault.description: Both parties consent to the divorce by filing Affidavits of Consent after 90 days from service of the complaint.
noFault.notes: Most common and fastest ground in Pennsylvania

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: The parties have lived separate and apart for at least one year and the marriage is irretrievably broken. (As amended effective December 2016; prior law required 2-year separation.)

fault.name: Willful and Malicious Desertion
fault.description: Respondent willfully and maliciously deserted Petitioner for one or more years.

fault.name: Cruel and Barbarous Treatment
fault.description: Respondent has by cruel and barbarous treatment endangered the life or health of Petitioner.

fault.name: Bigamy
fault.description: Respondent has knowingly entered into a bigamous marriage while a former marriage is still subsisting.

fault.name: Imprisonment for Crime
fault.description: Respondent has been sentenced to imprisonment for a term of two or more years upon conviction of a crime.

fault.name: Indignities to the Person
fault.description: Respondent has offered such indignities to the person of Petitioner as to render Petitioner's condition intolerable and life burdensome.

fault.name: Institutionalization for Serious Mental Disorder
fault.description: Respondent has been adjudged mentally ill and institutionalized for 18 or more months and there is no reasonable prospect of discharge within 18 months.

propertyDivision.description: Pennsylvania is an equitable distribution state. Marital property is divided equitably, not necessarily equally. The court considers 11 statutory factors.
factors: Age, health, station, amount and sources of income, vocational skills, employability, estate, liabilities and needs of each of the parties
Contribution by one party to the education, training or increased earning power of the other party
Opportunity of each party for future acquisitions of capital assets and income
Sources of income of both parties
Contribution of each party to the acquisition, preservation, depreciation or appreciation of marital property
Value of the property set apart to each party
Standard of living of the parties established during the marriage
Economic circumstances of each party at the time the division of property is to become effective
Tax ramifications associated with the proposed property division

alimony.description: The court may award alimony to either party. Pennsylvania also provides for Alimony Pendente Lite (APL) during the divorce proceedings.

alimonyPendenteLite.description: Temporary support paid during divorce proceedings

custody.statute: Pa. R.C.P. 1915.1 et seq. / 23 Pa.C.S. § 5321 et seq.
custody.description: Pennsylvania uses 'Legal Custody' and 'Physical Custody' terminology. Shared physical custody (equal time) is distinct from primary physical custody.

childSupport.description: Child support is calculated using the income shares model under Pennsylvania's statewide support guidelines.

affidavitOfConsent.name: Affidavit of Consent (mutual consent divorce)
affidavitOfConsent.notes: Both parties must file after 90-day waiting period

inventoryAndAppraisement.name: Inventory and Appraisement
inventoryAndAppraisement.notes: Required in some counties when property is contested

filingFees.notes: Varies by county. Fee waiver available for qualifying low-income individuals.

legalCitations.description: Grounds for divorce — no-fault (mutual consent § 3301(c); 1-year separation § 3301(d) as amended Dec. 2016) and fault-based grounds (§ 3301(a))
Alimony Pendente Lite — temporary support during proceedings
Child custody — legal and physical custody provisions

formattingRequirements.notes: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas follows local rules which may vary by county.

basic.name: Notice to Defend and Claim Rights
basic.description: Required notice informing defendant of rights and obligations

basic.name: Vital Statistics Certificate
basic.description: Required statistical information for the Department of Health

basic.name: Decree in Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Original Process (Service of Complaint)
service.description: Formal service of the divorce complaint on defendant

service.name: Acceptance of Service
service.description: Defendant accepts service without formal process
service.notes: Must be in writing and signed by defendant

withChildren.name: Income and Expense Statement
withChildren.description: Required financial disclosure for support claims

withChildren.name: Child Support Guidelines Calculation (Pa. R.C.P. 1910.16-4)
withChildren.description: Income shares calculation per Pennsylvania Child Support Guidelines

withChildren.name: Custody Complaint / Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Separate action or agreement for custody arrangement
withChildren.notes: Custody is a separate proceeding in Pennsylvania; may be filed concurrently

inState.description: Defendant must file a responsive pleading within 20 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Pennsylvania must file a responsive pleading within 20 days of service; additional time may be granted by the court

childSupportGuidelines.description: Pennsylvania uses an income shares model. Both parents' net monthly incomes are combined and matched to a basic support schedule. The obligation is then apportioned based on each parent's share of the combined net income. Adjustments are made for health insurance, childcare, mortgage/rent, and extraordinary expenses.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The guidelines are updated periodically by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court Domestic Relations Procedural Rules Committee.

options: County where the parties last cohabited
